tagline: A forested Bosphorus village famous for tulips, Ottoman gardens, and one of Istanbul's most beautiful parks — best visited in spring.

items.name: Emirgan Parkı Çay Köşkleri
items.description: Three restored Ottoman pavilions inside Emirgan Park serve tea and coffee with views of the Bosphorus and gardens. Genuinely beautiful.
items.tip: The yellow pavilion (Sarı Köşk) has the best terrace view. Go in autumn for the foliage — spectacular and far less crowded than tulip season.

items.name: Emirgan İskelesi Cafés
items.description: Small cafés by the ferry landing with Bosphorus views. A pleasant spot to wait for or watch the ferries.

items.name: Emirgan Sütis
items.description: A beloved local dairy café famous for its clotted cream (kaymak) breakfasts and traditional Turkish sweets. A neighbourhood institution.
items.tip: The kaymak and honey breakfast is extraordinary. Go on a weekday morning to avoid the weekend queues.

items.name: Emirgan Parkı
items.description: One of Istanbul's most beautiful Ottoman parks, famous for its tulip festival in April but gorgeous year-round. Three restored pavilions, forested hillsides, Bosphorus views.
items.tip: April tulip festival is spectacular but extremely crowded. Visit in October for golden foliage and peaceful paths.

items.name: Sakıp Sabancı Museum
items.description: One of Istanbul's finest private art museums in a stunning Bosphorus villa. Rotating international exhibitions of consistently high quality.

tips: Emirgan is best reached by bus from Beşiktaş or taxi from Sarıyer metro.
The tulip festival in April is Istanbul's most colourful annual event — but go very early or on a weekday.
Autumn is the best-kept secret: golden leaves, empty paths, and the same beautiful setting.
Walk south along the Bosphorus road to İstinye (about 20 minutes) for a pleasant combined visit.
